clue.text: For example, x and y across primarily, the other going vertically?

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of the word across
in a down entry, going vertically means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a bit of the other is a British euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: A maths lesson: one coordinate line runs across, the other runs up the page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going vertically' reverses SEX to XES, since this is a down clue read upwards. The whole clue also describes the answer: the x one goes across first, the y one vertically.
explanation.definitionFit: On a graph the x and y lines are the two reference lines, each one an example of such a line.

clue.text: Guided after party, leaving I supposed

indicators.note: after puts the word for guided behind the shortened party
leaving means the letter I goes out of the word for party

parts.note: a social is a party or gathering
guided means led

explanation.surface: Someone shown home after a party, and then the narrator was left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops I from SOCIAL, leaving SOCAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposed and the hyphenated phrase both mean 'commonly named but doubtfully so', as in a supposed expert.

clue.text: Ruin race

definitions.meaning: to ... hopes is to ruin them

explanation.surface: A terse note pairing wreckage with a running contest.
explanation.definitionFit: One word serves as a verb for wrecking plans and as a noun for a brief sprint.

clue.text: Praise cook having nailed hot drink

indicators.note: having nailed is read as having pinned something inside, so the drink sits within the cooking word

parts.note: to fry is to cook
a latte is a hot milky coffee

explanation.surface: A cook is complimented for getting the coffee just right.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive or insincere praise is the sense; compliments laid on thick.

clue.text: Brief batting appearance

parts.note: in cricket a side batting is said to be in
form can mean shape or appearance

explanation.surface: A cricketer's short stay at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective describing the innings, but it is a verb meaning to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: To brief someone is to tell them the facts, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Choice to make between altruism and greed — that's about right

definitions.text: Choice to make between altruism and greed
definitions.meaning: read literally, the phrase offers a choice between handing over and grabbing
means approximately, allowing a little either way

explanation.surface: A moral dilemma, then a shrug that the estimate is close enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Approximately is the idiom's everyday sense: a figure plus or minus a little.

clue.text: Louse up in cake

parts.note: to muff something is to bungle or louse it up

explanation.surface: An insect infestation discovered inside a bun.
explanation.definitionFit: A small baked sponge, often eaten at breakfast, is a kind of cake.

clue.text: See 23
Tongue with hot kiss rolling around, love it!

indicators.note: rolling around means the hot and kiss letters turn back to front

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A passionate snog, with an enthusiastic exclamation of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means a language; this is a Bantu language of South Africa.

clue.text: Covering golf, broadcast outlined distance, one way or another

indicators.note: covering means the scrambled letters wrap around the golf letter
broadcast means scattered, so the letters of outlined are rearranged

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golf broadcast describing how far a shot travelled.
explanation.definitionFit: This coordinate measures angular distance east or west of the Greenwich meridian, so either way.

clue.text: One stranded in Italian restaurant in squalid area east of resort

indicators.note: in an across entry, east of means placed to the right of the resort word

parts.note: a spa is a resort town
a ghetto is a run-down, squalid district

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in an Italian eatery in a seedy part of a holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranded' suggests marooned, but it means a single strand.
explanation.definitionFit: The singular of the pasta dish names one thin noodle, a single strand on the plate.

clue.text: Each foot initially grazed, swore

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of each and foot

parts.note: grazing animals fed

explanation.surface: An animal grazing grumbles as each hoof scrapes.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemistic past tense meaning used the F-word, so cursed.

clue.text: What 18 never wore when singing aloud, in essence?

definitions.text: What 18 never wore when singing aloud, in essence?

parts.words: What 18 never wore when singing aloud, in essence?
parts.note: 18 is the actor Yul Brynner; 'Yul never wore' plus the scent sounds like the song You'll Never Walk Alone, and the scent is an essence

explanation.surface: A question about what a bald film star did not put on.
explanation.walkthrough: Sung out, 'Yul never wore' plus the answer gives You'll Never Walk Alone, a football anthem from Carousel; 'in essence' points to perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: A light perfume made from essential oils, named after a German city.

clue.text: Seats, say, with black padding — stuff those in to fill out?

definitions.text: stuff those in to fill out?

indicators.note: padding means the black letter is stuffed inside the word for vehicles

parts.note: SEAT is a Spanish make of car, so Seats are examples of cars
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: Upholstery talk: seats padded, stuffing pushed in to plump them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seats' suggests upholstery but is the car brand SEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating plenty of starchy foods like bread and pasta is a way to put on weight.

clue.text: Defended by judge, other malcontents causing things to bubble up?

indicators.note: defended by means held within the words judge, other malcontents

explanation.surface: A judge protecting troublemakers who stir things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth's internal heat drives hot springs and geysers, which bubble up.

clue.text: Artificial satellite along with a — natural one?

parts.note: Mir was the Soviet space station
along with means and

explanation.surface: Comparing a man-made orbiter with a real moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A moon of Uranus, so a natural satellite as opposed to an artificial one.

clue.text: A sentry abandoning attempt to consume last bit of Cornish pasty

indicators.note: to consume means the shortened guard word swallows a letter
abandoning means the word for attempt leaves sentry

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: last bit of takes the final letter of Cornish

explanation.surface: A guard gives up trying to eat a Cornish pasty.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cornish pasty is a pastry turnover from Cornwall, but here 'pasty' is an adjective meaning pale; the noun reading is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasty means pale and unhealthy-looking; grey-white in the face.

clue.text: See 29
Deborah's king of cinema somewhat conciliatory, ultimately

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the words conciliatory, ultimately is used

explanation.surface: A film monarch who proves fairly peacemaking in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Brynner played the King of Siam opposite Deborah Kerr in The King and I.

clue.text: Party fringes in torment, ailing badly

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put together wrongly, so they are rearranged
fringes takes the outer letters of torment

explanation.surface: Someone ill and suffering at the edges of their agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins the two Ts from torment with AILING before 'badly' scrambles the lot. 'Party' is one side in a lawsuit, not a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A party to a lawsuit is one who sues or is sued.

clue.text: Cry of frustration, Vulcan finally out of hangar, malfunctioning

indicators.note: malfunctioning means what remains of hangar is jumbled
out of means that letter is removed from hangar
finally takes the last letter of Vulcan

explanation.surface: A Vulcan bomber breaks down as it finally leaves its hangar.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vulcan was a British jet bomber. 'out of' removes N from HANGAR, leaving HAGAR, which 'malfunctioning' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of exasperation, the noise made when things go wrong.

clue.text: Influential Russian beginning to rule presidentially?

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of rule

parts.note: acting presidentially in Russia is read as behaving as Putin

explanation.surface: Wondering if a Russian's ruling style is like a president's.
explanation.definitionFit: The mystic monk who held sway over the last Tsar's family.

clue.text: Endless condiment put on food, jump!

indicators.note: put on means the shortened condiment goes before the food in this across entry
endless means the last letter of the condiment is dropped

parts.note: salt is a condiment
chow is slang for food

explanation.surface: Seasoning food, then an order to leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure-skating jump, taking off from one skate's back inside edge.

clue.text: Reptile in charge, Britain's lowest point?

parts.note: a lizard is a reptile
the head is the person in charge

explanation.surface: A cold-blooded creature running the country's least impressive moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lowest' means southernmost on a map, not worst; the Lizard peninsula in Cornwall is the most southerly part of mainland Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The headland at the tip of the Lizard is the southernmost point of mainland Britain, its bottom on the map.

clue.text: Tin hat battered in conflict, people united, eh?

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the word for conflict

parts.note: war is conflict

indicators.note: battered means the letters of tin hat are knocked out of shape

parts.note: a nation is a people united under one state

explanation.surface: A dented helmet in wartime, with a nation pulling together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eh?' is the whole definition: the answer is an American folksy oath, a minced form of 'what in damnation'.
explanation.definitionFit: A folksy exclamation of bafflement, asking what on earth is going on.

clue.text: Crime rate, regrettably, male issue

indicators.note: regrettably suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of rate are rearranged

parts.note: issue means offspring, and male offspring is a son

explanation.surface: A sad statistic on offending, and a problem among men.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country is the gravest crime against the state.

clue.text: Catching last of fuzz, howl when that's pulled back?

definitions.text: Catching last of fuzz, howl when that's pulled back?

indicators.note: pulled back means the assembled letters are read in reverse
catching means the howl word holds a letter inside

parts.note: to roar is to howl

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of fuzz

explanation.surface: Shaving stubble and yelping as the blade is drawn back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catching' puts Z inside ROAR, making ROZAR, which 'pulled back' reverses. The whole clue also pictures a blade drawn over stubble with a yelp.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaving blade catches stubble and, pulled back over the skin, might make one cry out.

clue.text: Book in fact unopened

indicators.note: unopened means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a truth is a fact

explanation.surface: A volume found inside, in fact, still sealed.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old Testament book, named after a Moabite woman.

clue.text: Doctor in proctologist's area of expertise has little time for hallucinogen

indicators.note: in means the word for doctor goes inside the specialist's area

parts.note: a proctologist specialises in the rectum and anus
to doctor an animal is to geld or castrate it
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A rectal specialist too busy to bother with drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb meaning castrate, not a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: The street name for the drug PCP, a hallucinogen.

clue.text: Paul's companion, spineless parasite blowing top

indicators.note: blowing top means losing the first letter, the top in a down entry

parts.note: a fluke is a parasitic flatworm, an invertebrate so spineless

explanation.surface: A spineless hanger-on of Paul loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul is also the setter's pseudonym, but here it is the apostle.
explanation.definitionFit: The evangelist travelled with the apostle on his missionary journeys.

clue.text: Contrary attention-seeker, brunette, after short story for broadcaster

indicators.note: after puts the reversed part behind the shortened story
short means the last letter of the story word is dropped

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: contrary means the following pieces run the opposite way

parts.note: oi is a call to get attention
dark describes a brunette's hair

explanation.surface: A contrary show-off with dark hair, after a brief yarn, ends up on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A station given over to phone-ins and discussion is a type of broadcaster.

clue.text: See 24
Prey dipped into by rorqual's mouth, main diet?

indicators.note: dipped into by means the prey word has a letter dipped inside it

parts.note: a kill is the prey taken by a hunter

indicators.note: mouth takes the opening letter of rorqual's

explanation.surface: A whale scooping up its prey in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: A rorqual is a type of baleen whale; 'main' is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: These tiny crustaceans form the staple food of whales in the ocean.
